title: Priv: k8s master lifecycle Terraform 'guardian' module for safe upgrades and active health remediation
creator: Alex Chen
description: Build a reusable Terraform module (internal codename: guardian) that provisions the Kubernetes control-plane related AWS resources for Redwood Private EKS clusters in customer VPCs. Scope includes: VPC networking preflight checks, KMS and cross-account IAM wiring, EKS cluster bootstrap (control-plane attachments, OIDC provider, encryption config), and a pluggable set of healthcheck probes with automatic remediation hooks. Goal is zero-surprise upgrades: create_before_destroy patterns where safe, immutable identifiers for critical attachments, and preflight gating to avoid accidental KMS/IAM rotations. The module must be idempotent, testable in our CI sandbox, and expose hooks used by the Private upgrade operator for canary/rollout coordination.
acceptance_criteria: Module can provision a new EKS cluster resources in a customer VPC using a single terraform apply in our CI sandbox
Applying a minor config change keeps the cluster control-plane stable (no unnecessary deletion of KMS keys or IAM roles)
Module emits a healthscore metric (ok/warn/error) to CloudWatch/Prometheus and provides remediation hooks (SNS/Lambda or SSM runbook trigger)
Upgrade workflow: canary plan (1 cluster), promote to fleet using module flags; documented terraform flags for create_before_destroy and graceful node rotation
Automated preflight check fails fast on risky diffs (KMS key replacement, VPC CIDR overlap, missing cross-account trust) with clear remediation guidance
Module passes end-to-end integration tests in private-ci (terraform plan/apply/destroy) and has a reviewed GH PR with at least 2 approvals
tasks: Design module public API and variable set (inputs/outputs) - include optional remediation SNS topic and ssm_automation_document
Implement core resources: eks cluster resource wrappers, OIDC provider, encryption_config referencing existing or new KMS key
Add preflight null_resource checks and a `planguard` script that scans terraform plan for unsafe changes
Implement health probes: k8s API reachability, control-plane API latency, cloudformation stack drift checks, KMS key health
Wire remediation hooks: SNS -> Lambda that runs SSM documents to restart kube-apiserver-external proxies or reattach ENIs
Write integration tests (terraform + localstack for subset) and CI pipeline steps for private-ci
Create documentation: usage examples, upgrade playbook, rollback steps, and security considerations
Open GH PR and coordinate review with infra-security and platform teams
notes: 2025-02-16: Initial spike completed. PoC creates EKS cluster with encryption config and OIDC. Found issue: create_before_destroy on KMS alias caused temporary loss of access. Decided to avoid rotating KMS keys by default.
2025-02-20: Design decision - expose `kms_key_mode` variable with options ["use_existing","create_never","create_with_alias_preserve"]. Default = use_existing to reduce blast radius.
2025-02-24: Discussed remediation model with SRE: prefer push model (SNS+Lambda) for immediate fixes, but also provide SSM runbooks for manual recovery. Priya to prototype Lambda glue.
2025-02-27: Security review kickoff: infra-security requested explicit IAM policies that are least-privilege and documented KMS key grants; tagging policy required for audit logs.
2025-03-01: Implemented planguard script that rejects terraform plans which include KMS key_replacement, VPC CIDR shrink, or IAM role path changes. Plumbed into CI as blocking check.
2025-03-02: Created GH draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-modules/pull/412 (work in progress). Added unit tests for planguard.

2025-03-03: Manual integration run in sandbox success for create/apply/destroy with `kms_key_mode=use_existing`. Notable follow-ups: improve healthscore granularity and autoscaling of Lambda remediation concurrency.
